item.title: Gut microbe-derived trimethylamine shapes circadian rhythms through the host receptor TAAR5
item.description: Elevated levels of the gut microbe-derived metabolite trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) are associated with cardiometabolic disease risk. Initiation of the metaorganismal TMAO pathway begins when dietary choline and related metabolites are converted to trimethylamine (TMA) by gut bacteria. item.title: Human brain dynamics and spatiotemporal trajectories during threat processing
item.description: Functional MRI (fMRI) research has traditionally investigated task processing using static blocked or event-related designs. item.title: Single-cell transcriptomics identifies altered neutrophil dynamics and accentuated T-cell cytotoxicity in tobacco-flavored e-cigarette-exposed mouse lungs
item.description: Despite the growing public health threat of electronic cigarettes (e-cigs), the cell-specific immune responses to differently flavored e-cig exposure remain poorly understood. To bridge this gap, we characterized the lung immune landscape following acute nose-only exposure to flavored e-cig aerosols in vivo using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) in mice. item.title: Accelerated evolution in networked metapopulations of <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i>
item.description: Natural populations are often spatially structured, meaning they exist as metapopulations composed of subpopulations connected by migration.
